releases.name: 1 download manager 2.2.11
releases.body:
## What's new

**Windows**
- New link grabber, like JDownloader's: a batch paste (a list of links, or ranges like `file[001-120].zip`) and several downloads caught from the browser at once now gather in one list. Each link is checked for name and size, you tick what you want, pick a folder and download them together.
- Fixed browser downloads going missing: when several downloads were caught at once, each replaced the one before it. They now collect in the link grabber, and a magnet or torrent waits its turn.

**Browser extension**
- Files are handed to the app as soon as the browser sees the response, before its own download starts. On Firefox the browser's download is blocked completely; on Chrome and Edge it is cancelled almost instantly, with the download bubble hidden.
- The browser's cancelled copy is now always removed from its downloads list, and a copy that already finished is deleted.

releases.name: 1 download manager 2.2.10

**Android**

- New Display scaling option in Settings (Small, Default, Large, Larger) to resize the whole interface.

releases.name: 1 download manager 2.2.8
releases.body:
﻿## What's new

**Windows**

releases.name: 1 download manager 2.2.5
releases.body:
## What's new

**Browser extension**
- Catches downloads from any site. Before, links from sites outside a short built-in list were refused and left to the browser.
- Holds the browser's own copy the moment a download starts, so small files are no longer saved twice or missed. If the app is closed, the browser carries on as usual.
- Asks for fewer permissions (removed the unused `scripting` and `activeTab`).

**Windows**
- "Start minimized" now starts hidden in the system tray, with no taskbar button.
- Large cookie sets from signed-in sites no longer make a capture fail.

**Android**
- New Quick Settings tile, "Download copied link": copy a link anywhere, tap the tile, and it opens ready to add.
- Smaller download (about 12 MB less) from release shrinking.

releases.name: ThermalScope 1.1.0
releases.body:
## ThermalScope 1.1.0

**Install:** run `ThermalScope-Setup-1.1.0.exe` (per-user, no admin). Prefer portable? Unzip `ThermalScope-1.1.0-win-x64.zip`. The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen may ask you to confirm.

### New
- **Frame pacer** - limits a game's FPS with evenly spaced frames; live FPS/frame-time, frame graph, per-game limits, auto-detect, tray, start with Windows. DirectX 10/11/12, 64-bit; anti-cheat games are skipped.
- **In-game overlay** - rounded strip inside the game window (FPS range, frame line, CPU/GPU load and temperature), scalable.
- **Looks** - Scope, Glass, Depth, Flat; light/dark, six accents, three dial styles, auto or fixed interface scale.
- **Hotkeys** - configurable system-wide shortcuts.
- **CPU data without PawnIO** - Windows counters for clock/power; real die temperature via PawnIO (opt-in) or MSI Afterburner when running. The motherboard zone is never shown as CPU.
- **Updates** - in-app update check with delta packages (changed files only) and automatic rollback.

### Fixes
- FPS formula, re-attach after toggling, hook swap-chain creation, helper DLL integrity (hash-verified), PawnIO installer hardening.

Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. `manifest-1.1.0.json` is used to build the next delta.

releases.name: ThermalScope v0.1.0
releases.body:
# ThermalScope v0.1.0

Initial public release of ThermalScope, a portable Windows hardware monitor with a standalone DirectX 11/12 FPS monitor.

## Highlights

- CPU and GPU usage, temperatures, clocks, power, and sensor availability
- Optional one-time PawnIO setup flow for CPU sensor access
- Read-only FPS monitoring for user-selected 64-bit DirectX 11/12 processes
- No FPS cap, RTSS, or MSI Afterburner dependency
- Administrator manifest for native process attachment and sensor coverage

## Downloads

- `ThermalScope.exe` — self-contained single-file build
- `ThermalScope-win-x64.zip` — regular self-contained folder build

## Requirements and notes

- Windows x64
- Run as administrator for the FPS monitor and complete sensor coverage
- The FPS monitor is opt-in and may be blocked by anti-cheat protected games; it does not bypass anti-cheat
- A DirectX 11/12 game is required to produce a frame-rate reading

meta.description: Portable Windows hardware monitor with DirectX FPS monitoring

releases.name: Forget-it 1.3.2
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.3.2

Transactions now only track real, completed credits and debits.

- **Junk is rejected** before it reaches Transactions: ads and offers, cashback promos, newsletters (unsubscribe footers), forwarded mail (Fwd:, FW:, Re:, forwarded-message blocks), spam.
- **Not-yet-payments are skipped**: reminders, "will be debited", dues, failed or declined payments, money requests.
- **Authentic only**: a message needs a completed-payment word (debited, credited, paid, spent, received...) and an account, card, UPI or receipt marker. Promotional sender IDs (-P) and ordinary phone numbers are ignored unless the text names your account or card.
- **Gmail** sync leaves out Promotions, Social, Forums, spam and forwarded mail, and judges each mail on its subject and snippet.
- **Clean-up**: pull to refresh removes earlier junk entries that came from messages. Entries you typed in, categorised or noted are never removed.
- Subscriptions and loans are no longer created from promotional or forwarded text.
- Gmail sign-in error 8 (UNREGISTERED_ON_API_CONSOLE) now explains the Google Cloud setup.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.3.1
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.3.1

Fixes for the automatic subscriptions and loans.

- **EMIs no longer become subscriptions.** Payments to lenders (finance, finserv, capital, loan and similar names) and amounts that match a loan you already track are kept out of subscriptions.
- **Nothing is invented any more.** Anything the app only guesses (a repeating charge, a loan whose amount, rate or months are placeholders) is added **on hold**: not counted in totals, no reminders. A loan's notes say which numbers were read from your messages and which are placeholders to correct.
- **Check it, then Keep or Delete.** Items added by the app show a strip with Keep and Delete, and so does the notification. Delete also stops the same payments from bringing it back; deleting any subscription or loan now does that.
- **On hold** for any subscription: swipe a row right (swipe left still deletes), or switch off Active on its edit screen. Subscriptions now have a Delete button on the edit screen too.
- Gmail sign-in explains what is missing instead of showing Google's error code, and the README has the exact Google Cloud steps and this app's SHA-1.

If 1.3.0 added subscriptions or loans that are really EMIs, open the list and tap Delete on them.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.3.0
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.3.0

Subscriptions and loans are now added automatically.

- **One confirmation is enough**: a receipt or confirmation email, notification or SMS for a subscription (say a one-year Claude plan) creates the subscription with how much you paid, when you paid, the billing cycle, when it renews or ends, the card used, and the account or cancel link for known services. The payment is added to the Money ledger as well.
- **Repeated charges** become subscriptions automatically.
- **Loans from messages**: an EMI message with the amount and the months creates the loan, and so does the same EMI two months running (instalments already seen are marked paid). Loan terms are estimates and the loan says so.
- **Undo** button on every automatic addition, and Settings, Capture switches to turn either behaviour off.
- EMI reminders that say "due" (not "debited") are now understood, promotional messages are ignored, and nothing you already track is added twice.

Updating from 1.2.1 inside the app downloads a small patch. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.2.1
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.2.1

Adapts to every screen size.

- **Tablets, foldables and landscape**: screens 600 dp wide and up get a navigation rail on the left instead of the bottom bar, and content stays centred at a comfortable reading width.
- **Small phones**: the quick-action buttons shrink to fit and the tab bar shows icons only below 360 dp, so nothing is clipped.
- **Smoother scrolling** on the Money tab and Overview: spending totals are recalculated only when the data changes.
- Lists leave room below the last item so the add button never covers it.

Updating from 1.2.0 inside the app downloads a small patch. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.2.0
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.2.0

- **Category drill-down**: tap a category on the Money tab to see where it was spent, when and how much: the total and change against last month, a day-by-day chart with weekly totals, merchants ranked by spend, and every payment with its date. Edit a payment or set the category's limit from there.
- **Bills for stock**: the Stock camera button now reads a grocery bill and adds every item with its quantity automatically, or restocks items you already track. It understands lines such as "2 x 1.50 3.00", "Rice 5kg" and "Milk 1L", and ignores a bill you have already added.

Updating from 1.1.0 inside the app downloads a small patch. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.1.0
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.1.0

A money and budgeting section.

- **Money tab**: all incoming and outgoing transactions in one ledger, from SMS, email, Gmail, photos and entries you add yourself. Filter, search, edit, and look back month by month.
- **Where it went**: spending by category with the highest category called out, change against last month, and a six-month trend.
- **Budgets**: an overall monthly budget and per-category limits, what is left each day, a projection for the month, and alerts at 80 percent and when a limit is passed.
- **Auto-categories**: payments are sorted into categories automatically; fix one and it is remembered for that merchant.
- **Overview** now shows spending, the budget bar, income and your top categories. A new Spend shortcut adds a transaction in two taps.
- Salary and other credits now read the sender ("from ACME CORP").

Existing data is kept. Download the APK for your phone (most phones: arm64-v8a); updating from 1.0.1 inside the app downloads a small patch. Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.0.1
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.0.1

Fixes for installing and for allowing SMS and email access.

- **Unlock SMS and email access**: Android 13 and later lock these permissions for apps installed from a file. Settings, Capture now shows a step-by-step guide with an Open App info button, and the first-run prompt tells you when access was not granted.
- **Install help** added to the README: what to do when Play Protect or Android's developer check blocks the APK, and how to allow restricted settings.
- Update patches are now published for the architecture APKs, so updating from 1.0.0 downloads a few MB instead of the full app.

Download the APK for your phone (most phones: arm64-v8a). Checksums are in `SHA256SUMS`.

releases.name: Forget-it 1.0.0
releases.body:
# Forget-it 1.0.0

First public release. An Android app that keeps track of everything you pay for, mostly on your phone.

## What it does
- **Trackers**: subscriptions (with trials and cancel links), EMIs and loans with a full amortization schedule, bills and utilities with usual-amount and seasonal checks, and household stock with per-batch expiry and low-stock alerts.
- **Auto-capture**: reads payment SMS and email alerts on the device, optional read-only Gmail sync, price-change detection, and EMIs marked paid when a matching payment arrives.
- **Scan anything**: photo or screenshot of a bill, EMI message, subscription receipt or grocery receipt is read on the phone and sorted into the right tracker for you to review. Voice entry for stock.
- **Spreadsheets and backup**: Excel and CSV import and export, and a full backup zip with photos.
- **Reminders** with snooze, a weekly summary, a home-screen widget, biometric lock, and a colourful animated interface.
- **In-app updates** with small delta patches.

## Install
Download the APK for your phone and open it. Most phones need **forget-it-1.0.0-arm64-v8a.apk**. Older 32-bit phones need armeabi-v7a, emulators need x86_64, and the universal APK works everywhere but is larger.
Android may ask you to allow installs from your browser or file manager the first time.

## Check the download
`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksum of every APK. Updates only install over an app signed with the same release key.

## Good to know
- Gmail sync needs a Google Cloud OAuth client for `app.forgetit`; the steps are in the README. Everything else works without it.
- Photo and receipt reading is on-device and works best on clear, well-lit images.
- Loan terms read from a photo are estimates; open the loan to correct them.

meta.description: Offline Android tracker for subscriptions, EMIs and loans, bills, and household stock. Scans SMS, email, photos and spreadsheets on the phone.

releases.name: AppDash 1.2.4
releases.body:
Android: see Play Store updates and update several apps at once.

**Android**
- **Open Play updates** (top of Updates) goes straight to Play's own Updates list with Update all. It covers the many Play apps that ship a build per phone and publish no version other apps can read.
- **Update selected**: switch on several updates (or Select all) and update them in one go. F-Droid and GitHub updates install one after another inside AppDash (Android asks you to confirm each); selected Play apps open Play's update list at the end.
- F-Droid updates now download from f-droid.org and install in AppDash instead of only opening F-Droid.

**Windows**
- No changes; existing installs update with a tiny delta.

**Download**
- Windows: `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe`
- Android 11+: `AppDash-1.2.4.apk` (also offered as an in-app update)

The other files are the update feeds the apps read.

releases.name: AppDash 1.2.3
releases.body:
More hardware details for the Windows app.

**Windows**
- Rarely-used checkboxes are rocker switches; file-type bars on a disk's page are faders
- The chart's Disk space / Number of apps choice is a two-position slide switch
- Search types onto an LCD
- A disk's Used / Free / Total read as an engraved spec plate; gauges get E/F fuel marks
- Folder and disk scans count up on dot-matrix tape counters
- The title LCD flickers on at launch (skipped when Windows reduces motion)

**Android**
- No visible changes

**Download**
- Windows: `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe` (existing installs update with a small delta)
- Android 11+: `AppDash-1.2.3.apk` (also offered as an in-app update)

The other files are the update feeds the apps read.

releases.name: AppDash 1.2.2
releases.body:
Android now checks Play Store apps for updates too.

**Android**
- Updates → Check now reads each Play-installed app's current version from its public Play Store page. Newer versions show under "Updates available" with an Update button that opens the app in the Play Store.
- Many large apps ship a different build per phone, so Play lists them as "Varies with device" and publishes no single version. Those stay in the Play Store group with an Open button. (Google offers no public way for other apps to see those versions.)
- About 220 KB per Play app, only when you tap Check now.

**Windows**
- No changes; existing installs update with a tiny delta.

**Download**
- Windows: `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe`
- Android 11+: `AppDash-1.2.2.apk` (also offered as an in-app update)

The other files are the update feeds the apps read.

releases.name: AppDash 1.2.1
releases.body:
More hardware details for the Android app.

**Android**
- Key clicks you can feel on every button, and a detent tick on switches (follows your phone's touch-feedback setting)
- Select checkboxes are rocker switches; storage-by-type bars are faders with a cap
- App details read like an engraved spec plate
- The storage meter has E/F fuel marks, and the LCD flickers on at launch
- Home ends with a nameplate and speaker grille

**Windows**
- No changes; existing installs update with a tiny delta

**Download**
- Windows: `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe`
- Android 11+: `AppDash-1.2.1.apk` (also offered as an in-app update)

The other files are the update feeds the apps read.

releases.name: AppDash 1.2.0
releases.body:
AppDash now looks and feels like a piece of hardware.

**New look (Windows + Android)**
- Machined grey body with screwed-in modules, a dot-matrix LCD for page titles and a black edition for dark mode
- Storage gauges are analogue meters with a needle; charts are LED level meters
- A status LCD with live lights: winget, Chocolatey and running jobs on Windows; Usage/Files access and update checks on Android
- The theme button is a real toggle switch; loading spinners are tape reels
- Windows: press 1–6 to switch pages (printed on the menu keys) and / to search; disk cards are drive bays with an activity light

**Android: app updates**
- Checks F-Droid apps against F-Droid, and apps you link to a GitHub repo against that repo's latest release (installs the APK for your phone's CPU, verified by checksum)
- Play Store and other store apps open in their store to update

**Download**
- Windows: `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe` (existing installs update themselves with a small delta)
- Android 11+: `AppDash-1.2.0.apk` (the app also offers it as an in-app update)

The other files are the update feeds the apps read.

releases.name: AppDash 1.1.0
releases.body:
First public release.

**Windows** – download `AppDashApp-win-Setup.exe` and run it (installs for your user, no admin needed; adds the .NET 8 Desktop Runtime if missing). AppDash updates itself from this repo's latest release, using small delta packages when available. `AppDashApp-win-Portable.zip` runs without installing (no auto-updates).

**Android** (11 or newer) – download `AppDash-1.1.0.apk` and open it. Allow installs from your browser or file manager when asked. Google Play Protect may warn that it hasn't seen this developer before; choose *Install anyway* if you trust this build. Grant Usage access and All files access inside the app for sizes, screen time and the storage breakdown. Newer versions are offered in the app.

The other files (`*.nupkg`, `releases.win.json`, `RELEASES`, `assets.win.json`, `latest.json`) are the update feeds the apps read; you don't need to download them.
